metaTitle: Best Cordless Tool Combo Kits Compared (2026)
metaDescription: Cordless power tool combo kits compared by tool count, battery size, brushless motors and platform depth from DeWalt, Milwaukee, Ryobi and more.
expertTake: The DeWalt DCK240C2 drill and impact driver kit is the best starter combo for most buyers: two excellent tools, two batteries and a charger. The Milwaukee M18 8-tool kit is the best full-shop kit, with a hammer drill, saws, grinder and three batteries. The Ryobi P1819 6-tool is the value pick with a very deep platform. The BLACK+DECKER 4-tool is only for light household work. Buy the platform, not just the box.
introParagraphs: A combo kit bundles several cordless tools around one battery system, so the batteries and charger are shared and the per-tool price is far lower than buying each separately. The catch is that you are choosing a platform for years, because every future tool and battery will need to match.
Tool quality, battery size and platform depth matter more than the count on the box. This guide explains how to judge a kit, then points you to the top picks above and the reviews below.

products.name: DEWALT DCK240C2 20V MAX Drill and Impact Driver Combo Kit
products.description:
The DCK240C2 pairs a compact drill driver rated up to 300 unit watts out with an impact driver rated up to 1,400 in-lbs of torque, plus two batteries, a charger and a bag. Both tools have integrated LED lights with a 20 second delay, and the impact driver has a one-handed 1/4 inch hex chuck.

These two tools do most of the work in a home or shop: the drill makes holes, and the impact driver sinks screws and lag bolts without stripping. A two-tool kit costs less than a larger bundle, and you get two batteries, so one can charge while the other works. Compared with the DeWalt 10-tool kit, it gives up saws and lights but keeps the tools you use every day.

The platform is the big draw: DeWalt 20V MAX has a very deep tool line, so you can add a saw or sander later with the same batteries. Keep the batteries cool and store them partly charged. Add a circular saw bare tool later and you have a full starter shop, since the same batteries run it.
products.bestFor: First-time buyers who want two excellent core tools and room to grow.
pros: Drill up to 300 UWO and impact up to 1,400 in-lbs
cons: Only two tools in the box
Compact batteries limit runtime on big jobs

products.name: DEWALT DCK1021D2 20V MAX 10-Tool Brushless Combo Kit

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: 10 tools including saws, grinder and light

products.description:
The DCK1021D2 is a 10-tool DeWalt 20V MAX kit with brushless core tools, two batteries, a charger and two bags. It includes a compact reciprocating saw with a keyless blade clamp, a grinder with a quick-change wheel release and an LED work light.

Ten tools cover remodeling, DIY and basic trade work: drilling, driving, cutting, grinding and lighting. Two batteries run all ten tools, which is the economy of a combo kit, though a single pair of packs cannot run every tool at once. Compared with the Milwaukee M18 8-tool, the DeWalt gives more tools but fewer batteries, and the Milwaukee adds a third compact pack.

Check the battery capacity in your listing, since sizes vary by bundle. Plan on a third battery if you will run saws and a grinder in the same session. Buy a third battery if you will run the saw and grinder back to back, since two packs cannot keep up with ten tools in a long session.
products.bestFor: Homeowners and remodelers who want a broad set in one purchase.
pros: Ten tools covering drilling to lighting
Brushless motors on the core tools
Keyless blade and quick-change wheel systems
cons: Two batteries for ten tools is thin
Some tools in big kits are lighter duty

products.name: Milwaukee M18 8-Tool Combo Kit with 3 Batteries

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Hammer drill, impact driver, circular saw, angle grinder, reciprocating saw, multi-tool, light

products.description:
The Milwaukee M18 8-tool kit includes a hammer drill, impact driver, circular saw, angle grinder, reciprocating saw, multi-tool and work light, plus three batteries (two high-capacity and one compact), a rapid charger and two heavy-duty contractor bags.

The tool list is the strongest in the guide: a hammer drill handles masonry, the grinder and reciprocating saw cover demolition and metal, and the circular saw cuts framing. Three batteries means you can run tools while two charge, which matters on a job site. Compared with the Ryobi P1819, the Milwaukee tools are built for professional duty cycles, and the M18 platform is among the deepest, with over 175 tools in a related Milwaukee listing.

It is the priciest kit here by a wide margin. If you do not need professional durability, a lighter platform gets you most of the way. Learn the tool bags layout before a job, since eight tools and three batteries pack tightly, and keep the compact battery for the drill and light.
products.bestFor: Contractors and serious DIYers who want job-site-grade tools in one bundle.
pros: Hammer drill, saws and grinder in one kit
Three batteries and a rapid charger
M18 has a very deep tool line
cons: Costs far more than consumer kits

products.name: RYOBI P1819 18V ONE+ 6-Tool Combo Kit

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Drill driver, impact driver, reciprocating saw, circular saw, multi-tool, LED light

products.description:
The Ryobi P1819 is a six-tool ONE+ kit with a drill driver, impact driver, reciprocating saw, circular saw, multi-tool and LED light, powered by one 4.0Ah and one 1.5Ah battery with a charger and bag. The ONE+ platform has over 125 tools in the listing, and they all work with any ONE+ 18V battery.

The battery mix is the compromise: a 4.0Ah pack runs a saw reasonably well, and the 1.5Ah pack is a light backup for a drill. The tools are DIY grade, not trade grade, but the kit costs a fraction of the DeWalt or Milwaukee kits. The deep platform means later purchases of outdoor tools, vacuums and lights share the same batteries.

For weekend projects this is an excellent value. Expect to buy a larger battery if you cut a lot. Add a 4.0Ah or larger pack early, since the 1.5Ah pack is best kept as a spare for the drill.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want the broadest, most affordable platform.
pros: Six useful tools in one kit
Low cost for the tool count

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 CMCK700D2 7-Tool Combo Kit

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Drill, impact driver, reciprocating saw and four more

products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN V20 CMCK700D2 is a seven-tool kit with two batteries, a charger and accessories. The drill is rated at 280 UWO with a two-speed gearbox, the impact driver at 1,460 in-lbs, 2,800 RPM and 3,100 BPM, and the reciprocating saw has a 1 inch stroke at 3,000 strokes per minute.

The specs sit close to the DeWalt starter tools: 280 UWO against DeWalt's 300, and 1,460 in-lbs against 1,400. The tool-free blade release on the recip saw is a thoughtful feature. The V20 platform is a homeowner line, with a good range of garage and outdoor tools, and it is less deep than DeWalt's or Milwaukee's.

For household use it is a strong value, and seven tools cover most projects. For heavy daily work, step up in durability. Check the blade release and chuck on arrival, since homeowner-grade tools show their wear first at the moving parts.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a seven-tool kit with strong drill and impact specs.
pros: Tool-free blade release on the recip saw
cons: Smaller platform than DeWalt or Milwaukee

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BD4KITCDCRL 20V MAX 4-Tool Combo Kit

specList.label: Tools
specList.value: Drill driver, circular saw, work light, one more

products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER 4-tool kit has a drill driver with a 3/8 inch chuck, 0 to 650 RPM and an 11-position clutch, a 5.5 inch circular saw with tool-free depth and bevel settings, a work light with up to 11 hours of runtime and a fourth tool, plus two batteries and a charger.

This is a consumer kit: the 3/8 inch chuck and 650 RPM top speed handle furniture assembly and light drilling, and the 5.5 inch saw cuts 2x lumber but with less depth than a 6-1/2 inch blade. The 11-position clutch protects screws and soft materials. Compared with the Ryobi or CRAFTSMAN kits, it has fewer tools and lighter motors.

It is a very affordable way to start a household tool collection. Do not expect to build a deck with it. Treat it as a starter kit for assembly and small repairs, and move to a stronger platform if your projects grow.
products.bestFor: Light household repairs and furniture assembly.
pros: Lowest cost of any kit here
cons: 3/8 inch chuck and 650 RPM limit the drill

buyingCriteria.explanation: The kit is a down payment on a platform. Ryobi ONE+ lists over 125 tools, Milwaukee M18 over 175 in a related listing, and DeWalt 20V MAX hundreds. Pick the platform with the outdoor and specialty tools you will want. Batteries do not cross brands. Look at the next three tools you want and check that the platform sells them.

A kit is only as good as its drill and impact driver, because you will use those most. The DeWalt DCK240C2 drill is rated up to 300 UWO and the impact up to 1,400 in-lbs, and the CRAFTSMAN impact driver is rated 1,460 in-lbs. Judge the pair first, and treat the extra tools as bonuses. Hold the drill and impact driver in the store if you can.

Two small batteries cannot run ten tools. The Milwaukee kit includes three, and the Ryobi uses 4.0Ah and 1.5Ah. Aim for at least one 4.0Ah pack for saws. A larger battery weighs more but cuts more. A kit with one big battery and one small one is a compromise, so check which sizes you get.

Brushless motors are more efficient and last longer. The DeWalt 10-tool kit uses brushless on its core tools. Brushed motors cost less but wear out sooner under heavy use. Check the motor type in the listing, since brand names do not guarantee brushless.

A ten-tool kit sounds like a bargain, but you may never use a grinder or multi-tool. A two-tool kit with better tools can be a better buy. Count the tools you will actually use. Be honest about which tools you will use before you pay for them.

A bag keeps a kit together. The Milwaukee kit has two contractor bags, and the DeWalt 10-tool has two. A kit with no bag lives in a box. Soft bags are easier to carry and store. A soft bag that holds every tool saves hours of hunting.

specDecoder.meaning: Unit watts out is a DeWalt power figure for the motor output. DeWalt lists 300 UWO for the DCK240C2 drill, and CRAFTSMAN lists 280 UWO. Use it to compare kits, not to predict real-world results.
specDecoder.watchFor: UWO is a manufacturer measure and not a standard across brands.

specDecoder.meaning: Torque is twisting force. An impact driver at 1,400 to 1,500 in-lbs sinks big screws and lag bolts. Use it to compare kits, not to predict real-world results.
specDecoder.watchFor: Peak impact torque is not the same as drill torque.

specDecoder.meaning: Blows per minute describe how often an impact driver hammers. Higher BPM drives faster in tough fasteners. Use it to compare kits, not to predict real-world results.
Strokes per minute describe how fast a reciprocating saw blade moves. The CRAFTSMAN is rated 3,000 SPM. Use it to compare kits, not to predict real-world results.
specDecoder.watchFor: Stroke length matters too, since a longer stroke cuts more per cycle.

specDecoder.meaning: Amp-hours show battery capacity. A 4.0Ah pack runs about twice as long as a 2.0Ah pack. Use it to compare kits, not to predict real-world results.
specDecoder.watchFor: Kits often include a mix of sizes. Check the listing.

cards.label: Small kit (2 to 4 tools)
cards.text: Better tools per dollar and less clutter. The DEWALT DCK240C2 and BLACK+DECKER 4-tool fit here.

cards.label: Big kit (6 to 10 tools)
cards.text: More variety and a lower per-tool price. The DEWALT 10-tool, Milwaukee 8-tool, Ryobi 6-tool and CRAFTSMAN 7-tool fit here.

howToChoose.note: Pick a small kit if you want quality and a big kit if you want variety.

maintenance.why: A fully drained pack may not recover. Top up every few months. It takes minutes and prevents most failures.
Heat shortens life. Do not leave them in a hot truck. It takes minutes and prevents most failures.
Dust clogs vents and chucks. Blow them out. It takes minutes and prevents most failures.
Dull blades overwork the motor and batteries. It takes minutes and prevents most failures.
A damaged charger is a fire risk. Replace it. It takes minutes and prevents most failures.

faq.a: Yes, because the per-tool price is lower and the batteries are shared. The risk is getting tools you do not use. A good habit is to price the tools you want to add later before you pick a platform.

Milwaukee and DeWalt lead for professionals, and Ryobi and CRAFTSMAN lead for value. Choose the platform with the tools you want. Look at the weight in the hand, since a heavy tool tires you faster than a slightly less powerful one.
Brushless tools last longer and run longer per charge. For occasional use, brushed tools are fine. Brushless also means no brushes to replace, which matters if you plan to keep the tools ten years.

faq.q: How many batteries do I need?
faq.a: Two is enough for most home use. A pro running saws needs three or more. Add a third battery if you work more than a few hours at a time.
Not batteries. Tools from different brands need their own packs and chargers. If you already own batteries from one brand, buy bare tools of that brand instead.
Bare tools are cheaper if you already own batteries. Kits include batteries and a charger. Bare tools also let you pick the exact battery size you want.
